result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-030.md for WF02-REQ-030 (walk-in registration at the door) at branch feature/WF02-REQ-030, base commit d8b1a73. Scope test: Step 2's artifacts_out (new domain/walkin.ts -- parseWalkinArgs/validateWalkinFields/normalizePhoneForMatching/decideWalkinOutcome/commitWalkin/formatWalkinConfirmMessage/formatWalkinOverrideMessage/parseWalkinMessageFields; domain/user.ts's extended getUserIdByPhone/createWalkinUser; domain/profile.ts's extended createWalkinProfile; new handlers/walkin.ts's 4 handlers; index.ts's new /walkin command + 3 callback wirings; new walkin.* i18n keys) is real behavioral surface -- a real /walkin command plus real button taps writing real users/profiles/registrations/audit_log rows. Full Steps 3b/4 apply.

Read core-directives.md, WF-02 Step 3, qa_testing_guide.md, docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-029.md as reference shape, docs/agents/design/REQ-030.md in full, apps/bot/src/domain/walkin.ts and apps/bot/src/handlers/walkin.ts in full (the real implementations), and BACKEND-DEV's already-committed apps/bot/src/handlers/walkin.db.test.ts in full (7 tests: 1xAC1, 1xAC2, 2xAC3, 1xAC4, 1xAC5, 1xAC6) so this spec's own cases are independently parameterized, not duplicates. Confirmed via grep that walkin.db.test.ts never references staleMessage or parseWalkinMessageFields (zero coverage of the malformed-message path), and confirmed no log.*/console.* call site exists anywhere in domain/walkin.ts or handlers/walkin.ts (both grepped directly) -- used this fact to design AC5's static check rather than a vacuous dynamic log-capture harness that would pass regardless of whether the flow ever logs anything.

Per-case design, all for a SECOND, NEW test file this spec designs, apps/bot/src/handlers/walkin.forgery.test.ts -- THIS FILE DOES NOT EXIST YET. Per this project's established convention (checkinQr.forgery.test.ts for REQ-029, checkin.forgery.test.ts for REQ-028), TEST-DESIGNER writes the markdown design only; TEST-RUNNER writes and commits the actual vitest file at Step 4 once this design passes Step 3b. Own nextTgId=943_000_000+ range, confirmed distinct from every existing file's range via grep -rn "nextTgId = " apps/bot/src (800M/900M/920M/940M/941M/942M[checkinQr.forgery.test.ts AND walkin.db.test.ts -- BACKEND-DEV's own committed file, the one range this spec must not collide with]/950M/960M/970M/980M/990M/1000000900).

- AC1: own fixture (Yerlan Toktarov/+996555112233), plus a column-level check on the organizer's OWN profile row before/after (not just row counts) -- catches a userId-resolution bug that overwrites the organizer's own profile in place without changing any table's row count, which a count-only check (BACKEND-DEV's own AC1 shape) cannot catch.
- AC3: own capacity-1 fixtures for both the override-confirm case (Bota Suleimenova -> Ruslan Abenov) and a SEPARATE dismiss-case fixture (Damir Zhaksybekov -> Aliya Mamedova), the dismiss case additionally querying audit_log directly for zero registration.walkin_admit/walkin_override_admit rows referencing the dismissed person -- BACKEND-DEV's own dismiss case never queries audit_log at all, only registration row counts.
- AC4: own two-differently-formatted-phone fixture verified to actually digit-strip-collide (+77074445566 vs 7 707 444-55-66, both -> 77074445566, confirmed via a direct node -e run of the normalization regex), independent of BACKEND-DEV's own chosen pair, plus the same company-not-overwritten assertion BACKEND-DEV's case makes, re-derived from an independent fixture.
- AC5: own fixture (Saltanat Yerbolova/+996700998877) covering BOTH the plain-admit and the override-admit audit payload shapes (BACKEND-DEV's own case only covers plain-admit) for the dynamic no-phone-in-payload check, PLUS a dedicated static check (git grep for log./console. call sites in the two implementation files, expected zero matches) as the genuine fail-able proof of S11 for this flow, reasoned explicitly in the spec for why a dynamic log-capture harness would be vacuous here (nothing in this flow ever calls the logger today).
- AC6: own fixture makes the acting user a GENUINE EventStaff row for this exact event (via addEventStaff), not merely a plain member with no staff role anywhere (BACKEND-DEV's fixture) -- this is the only fixture shape that could catch a regression accidentally accepting EventStaff membership as sufficient for a walk-in add (S2/design §4's organizer-only gate).
- Cross-context forgery (new, no existing coverage): two-chapter fixture where Chapter A's organizer taps a confirm message's own button (real callback_data + real captured message text) that was rendered for Chapter B's event by Chapter B's own organizer -- verifies eventId comes only from callback_data (never re-parsed text, which carries no eventId at all) and that requireOrganizerForChapter re-derives fresh from the TAPPING user's own chapter membership. Explicitly reasoned in the spec why one case against the confirm tap suffices (the override tap's §8.3 inherits the identical re-authorization call, §8.2 steps 1-5 verbatim -- no distinct code path a second case could catch).
- Malformed/corrupted message text (new, no existing coverage, per this run's task brief): a callback dispatched with a hand-corrupted message.text missing the "Phone: " line (and, as a second cheap assertion in the same test, missing "Name: " instead) -- verifies parseWalkinMessageFields's { ok: false } branch produces a clean staleMessage refusal, no crash, no write, and specifically that commitWalkin (and its own resolve-or-create step) is never reached at all in this case, which BACKEND-DEV's own suite has zero coverage of (grep-confirmed).

AC2 deliberately not re-covered: BACKEND-DEV's own committed case already drives through real dispatch with adequate own-fixture coverage (admission/checkedInAt/checkInMethod/success-message assertions), no gap found reading walkin.db.test.ts directly, mirroring REQ-029's own precedent for not re-covering an AC with no found gap.

Stated the --no-file-parallelism requirement (ISS-0014) for TEST-RUNNER. Filed one incidental finding for ORCH to issue-queue: checkinQr.forgery.test.ts (not-yet-written, per REQ-029's own spec) and walkin.db.test.ts (already committed by BACKEND-DEV) both declare nextTgId = 942_000_000 -- a pre-existing latent collision risk in this codebase's test-range convention, not this run's task to fix, not currently causing a failure under --no-file-parallelism's per-file truncation discipline. No implementation defect found in the read domain/walkin.ts or handlers/walkin.ts code while reading it directly for this step.

issues.description: apps/bot/src/handlers/checkinQr.forgery.test.ts (REQ-029's not-yet-written spec) and apps/bot/src/handlers/walkin.db.test.ts (BACKEND-DEV's already-committed REQ-030 file) both declare `let nextTgId = 942_000_000`, a duplicate tgId range across two files. Not currently causing a failure (each DB-backed file truncates all relevant tables in its own beforeEach and files run --no-file-parallelism per ISS-0014), but a latent footgun for the next file copied from either as a template. Recommend ORCH file this as its own ISS-NNNN for whichever agent next touches either file to fix by re-picking a free range.
